tour.title: Project Bootstrap & Package Management
tour.description: The entry point to this dotfiles repo is setup.sh, which orchestrates the entire deployment: it installs Homebrew bundles from Brewfile (84 formulae + 21 casks), decrypts secrets with age, and symlinks config files into place. The .zshrc ties everything together at shell startup — loading plugins (autosuggestions, syntax-highlighting, vi-mode), sourcing decrypted secrets from env.secrets.age, and initializing tools like starship, atuin, and zoxide. Together these files form the foundation that all other tools depend on.

tour.title: Shell Environment & Terminal Multiplexer
tour.description: The shell experience is shaped by three configs: starship.toml customizes the prompt with a moonfly color palette and module styling for git, languages, and directory context. The .tmux.conf configures tmux with Ctrl-a prefix, vi copy mode, session management via sesh+fzf, and TPM plugins (vim-tmux-navigator, resurrect, continuum, yank). The tmux-sessionizer.conf adds quick-session commands and defines search paths under $HOME/repos. Together these create a fast, vi-centric terminal workflow.

tour.title: Neovim Core: Init, Plugin Manager, Keymaps & Options
tour.description: Neovim is built on LazyVim. The init.lua entry point bootstraps the plugin manager via lazy.lua, which sets up lazy.nvim, imports LazyVim defaults, and loads all plugin specs from lua/plugins/. The keymaps.lua file defines custom bindings for split management, scroll centering, terminal toggle, and paste-without-overwrite. The options.lua configures relative line numbers, treesitter folding, persistent undo, the moonfly colorscheme, and disables LSP logging and diagnostic virtual text. These four files establish the editor's behavior and extensibility model.

tour.title: Neovim Plugins: LSP, Completion, Syntax & Formatting
tour.description: The core editing intelligence comes from four plugin specs. lspconfig.lua configures language servers (tailwindcss, vtsls, eslint, typos_lsp) with custom keymaps for rename, unused-import removal, and ESLint fix. blink-cmp.lua provides fast autocompletion with custom sources including avante, dadbod, and supermaven. treesitter.lua ensures 25+ language parsers are installed with auto-install for missing ones. conform.lua maps filetypes to formatters (prettier, stylua, shfmt). Together these deliver IDE-grade code intelligence inside the terminal.

tour.title: Neovim Plugins: UI, Git, AI & Workflow
tour.description: Beyond core editing, several plugins shape the daily workflow. colorscheme.lua activates the moonfly colorscheme used consistently across all tools. fzf.lua provides fuzzy finding for files, grep, and git branches. diffview.lua adds git diff browsing with file/branch history. The opencode.lua and supermaven.lua specs integrate AI coding assistants directly into the editor. The disabled.lua file is notable — it selectively disables LazyVim defaults (bufferline, mini.surround, flash, noice, trouble) to keep the setup lean and intentional.

tour.title: Terminal Emulators & Window Management
tour.description: Two terminal emulators are configured — ghostty/config uses Fira Code at 16pt with a custom moonfly 16-color palette and disabled ligatures, while kitty/kitty.conf uses the same font with a Catppuccin Mocha-inspired scheme. The .aerospace.toml configures AeroSpace, a macOS tiling window manager, with keybindings for workspace navigation, window movement, layout switching, and a service mode. The moonfly color theme flows consistently from the terminal emulators through to the window manager's visual identity.

tour.title: Yazi File Manager: Config, Theme & Plugins
tour.description: The Yazi terminal file manager is configured through four files. yazi.toml defines the main settings for layout, preview, openers, and tasks. keymap.toml maps keyboard shortcuts for all UI components. theme.toml selects the moonfly flavor for visual consistency. The init.lua entry point loads two custom plugins: git.yazi (shows git status signs with bubble-up/propagate-down logic) and bookmarks.yazi (vi-like marks with save/jump/delete and persistence). The moonfly flavor (flavor.toml + tmtheme.xml) provides a comprehensive color scheme covering all UI components, filetype rules, and an extensive icon set.

tour.title: Dashboard, AI Tools & Custom Tooling
tour.description: The Glance dashboard (glance.yml) creates a home page with three columns: clock/calendar/todo/stocks, RSS feeds from engineering blogs and YouTube channels, and weather/Pi-hole/torrent/GitHub widgets. On the AI tooling side, opencode.json configures the OpenCode coding assistant with a Gemini auth plugin, while gemini/index.ts implements an image generation/editing/analysis tool using Gemini 2.5 Flash. The task-management skill (router.sh + task-cli.ts) provides a CLI for tracking feature subtasks with dependency resolution and validation. A consistent moonfly theme (moonfly.json) unifies the OpenCode TUI with the rest of the dotfiles.
